subject: Order Form negotiation: heartbeat availability metric, pro-rated credits & maintenance carveouts
messages:
From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@atlascloud.com>
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@atlascloud.com, j.ellis@atlascloud.com
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 20:22:00 -0800
Subject: AtlasCloud redlines (Order Form + SLA) — initial pass

Hi Sofia / Marissa,

Attached are AtlasCloud's redlines to the Order Form and MSA focused on availability and support terms. Two items they flagged specifically: (1) how uptime is measured — they want a "heartbeat"-style per-customer check to be the source-of-truth, and (2) service credits should be prorated to the minute with a cap and an explicit remediation ladder.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept a heartbeat metric (or provide our telemetry equivalent), and whether you have a sliding credit scale we can align on? Procurement would also like any proposed maintenance blackout windows and a short statement about emergency patch protocols.

Attached: atlascloud_redlines_v1.docx

Thanks — Maya
Maya Singh
Sr. Procurement Manager, AtlasCloud
procurement@atlascloud.com

From: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@atlascloud.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: AtlasCloud redlines (Order Form + SLA) — initial pass

Maya — thanks for sending this over. We reviewed the redlines and have initial positions below. We're happy to sync on a quick call but wanted to capture our thinking first so legal/engineering have something concrete to react to.

1) Heartbeat metric: Redwood can expose a customer-specific availability signal derived from our telemetry ("heartbeat"). By default we propose our internal telemetry as the source-of-truth with the option for AtlasCloud to supply synthetic checks; we can accept either as evidence for a credit claim provided the check meets agreed probe definitions (location/interval).

2) Measurement window: monthly rolling 30-day window. Availability is calculated as (minutes up / total minutes in window) at the tenant level.

3) Proposed uptime tiers and credit ladder (suggested):
   - >= 99.95%: no credit
   - 99.50% - 99.94%: 10% credit of monthly service fees
   - 99.00% - 99.49%: 25% credit
   - < 99.00%: 50% credit (cap)
   Cap: Credits applied capped at 50% of monthly recurring service fees. Credits are prorated to the minute to reflect actual downtime.

4) Maintenance windows: regular maintenance window proposed Sun 02:00–04:00 UTC. Emergency patches: Redwood may perform emergency patches with a maximum expected disruption of 4 hours; we will provide notice as soon as feasible and a post-incident report. Emergency patch carveouts to credits will be allowed where customer-impacting work is required for security/compliance.

5) Evidence & transparency: For credit claims we will provide telemetry snapshots, incident timeline, and audit logs. AtlasCloud may submit their synthetic check logs; if there's a discrepancy, both logs are reviewed and mutually agreed reconciliation applies.

I've attached a short redline suggestion with language for the Order Form. If this looks acceptable we can circulate to Legal.

Attachments: redline_suggestion_sofia.docx

Next steps: propose 30-minute call Mon/Tue next week to walk through the credit ladder and heartbeat probe definition.

— Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Head of Customer Contracts, Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@atlascloud.com>, sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 11:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: AtlasCloud redlines (Order Form + SLA) — legal redline proposals

Thanks — Sofia and Maya. Legal reviewed the suggested ladder and we propose the following clean-up and an explicit calculation clause to avoid disputes. I'm pasting a short redline excerpt below for your team to review; full redline attached.

--- suggested Order Form excerpt (redline) ---
"Availability Measurement and Credits: Availability shall be measured on a rolling 30-day period at the Tenant level. 'Available' means the Service responds to customer TLS requests or, where agreed, the customer's configured synthetic heartbeat probe, within expected protocol thresholds. If Availability for the 30-day period falls below the tiers set forth below, Customer will be eligible for the indicated Service Credit(s):
  a) 99.95% or greater — No credit
  b) 99.50% to 99.94% — 10% of monthly fees
  c) 99.00% to 99.49% — 25% of monthly fees
  d) Less than 99.00% — 50% of monthly fees (maximum aggregate credits per month).
Service Credits shall be calculated as a percentage of the monthly recurring fees and will be prorated to the minute. Customer must submit a credit claim within 30 days of the end of the measurement period. Credits are Customer's sole and exclusive remedy for Availability failures.
--- end excerpt ---

Legal also suggests we add: (i) an explicit 30-day submission window for claims, (ii) cap aggregate credits to 50% of the fee for the period, and (iii) a carveout that credits do not apply to scheduled maintenance that was announced 72 hours in advance nor to emergency security patches.

Please review; Maya — does AtlasCloud agree to a 30-day claims window and 72-hour maintenance notice carveout?

Marissa Cole
Sr. Counsel, Contracts, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 08:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: AtlasCloud redlines — engineering feasibility notes

Quick technical note from infra:

- Heartbeat: we can publish a tenant-level heartbeat metric derived from our internal edge and routing telemetry. This will be the most consistent and tamper-resistant source. If AtlasCloud wishes to provide their synthetic checks, we can accept them as supplementary evidence but require probe definitions (probe frequency, geographic origin, expected timeout).

- Measurement: minute-level granularity is straightforward, but rolling 30-day windows mean we need to retain minute-level availability for 31 days for reconciliation; cost of storage/retention is nominal and fine.

- Credits calc: prorating to the minute is trivial once we have the availability minutes count. However, we recommend capping credits (50%) to prevent operational risk.

- Emergency patch window: we support a 4-hour expected disruption for critical security patches but will try to keep impact < 30 minutes. For mutual clarity, engineering will provide a post-patch incident report within 48 hours.

Happy to join the call to explain telemetry and how the heartbeat is computed (edge vs region vs global).

— Aditya
Aditya Rao
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.ai

Maya — thank you. Based on the thread above Legal is comfortable with the proposed ladder, the 30-day rolling window, 30-day claim submission, and the 72-hour scheduled maintenance notice carveout. We will accept the heartbeat metric as Redwood telemetry by default with AtlasCloud synthetic checks admissible as supporting evidence (probe definitions required).
